summary: Stellar Odyssey is a game where you’re in charge of figuring out whether an asteroid is going to hit Earth and what to do about it. You’d have limited money and time, so you’d have to choose between researching it more, getting better equipment, or launching a mission to change its path. The catch is you wouldn’t know how dangerous it actually is at first, so acting too early could waste your money, but waiting too long could mean missing your chance. Picture a mission-control dashboard with a moving space map, research options, and updates as you make decisions. We could build it as a 2D browser game using React and TypeScript and use NASA information to help design the scenario. We could also add a rewind feature so players can see how a different choice would’ve changed the outcome. That way, it’s not just another game where you shoot asteroids you actually have to think through your decisions.
details: The Stellar Odyssey is a strategy game where players have limited time, a budget, and have to make difficult choices to deflect an asteroid. You have to decide how much money you want to spend on researching, deflection with a spacecraft, and getting better equipment. You have to make choices at the correct time and it teaches others how people at mission control over at NASA might deal with these situations. Our project is different because instead of deciding to build a spacecraft and send it to observe or sample a planet, we stay on earth and send spacecrafts to stop it. We had considered having a normal space mission design but it had seemed like everyone else would do it and like it was an obvious answer. We knew that we could do better and somehow built off of the idea of mission control.
